title: coyodex project map
description: Auto-generated from tools/coyodex/model.py — documentation and IDE-autocomplete use only; NOT used by `coyodex validate` (see this module's docstring, and method/model.md, for why). Regenerate with `python -m coyodex.json_schema > method/project-map.schema.json`.

commit.description: short commit sha the map was built at.

tool_commit.description: short commit sha of the COYODEX build that produced this map — not the analysed repo's. Two maps are only comparable against the tools that made them; absent on maps built before this was stamped.

id.description: a role is a first-class element (`R<n>`), referenced by id — a use case's `actors` and a flow's actor steps carry role ids.

kind.description: human | service, free text (not a closed vocabulary).

drives.description: the use cases this role drives — free text, ids inside.

source.description: either a bare file `path:line` anchor (see `evidence[].file`'s description) or a bare directory ref ending in `/`. The term's canonical code home (where it is defined); null when the concept has no single code home (a pure product-level term).

id.description: `S<n>` in subsystems[], `SD<n>` in subdomains[], `CAP<n>` in capabilities[], `BLK<n>` in blocks[] — same dataclass, four id forests.

parent.description: the enclosing group's id, in the SAME forest (an S parents an S, an SD an SD, a CAP a CAP, a BLK a BLK), or null for top-level.

label.description: CAPABILITY-ONLY: an authored judgement about the use cases in this capability — core is the product and the Happy Path walks every core capability. Nothing derives it, and `validate` blocks it on a subsystem or a subdomain.

source.description: either a bare file `path:line` anchor (see `evidence[].file`'s description) or a bare directory ref ending in `/`. The group's home directory (or a representative file).

confidence.description: verified = read in the code; inferred = deduced. '' = unstated.

tech.description: SUBSYSTEM-ONLY: one honest stack label ('Python/FastAPI', 'Go', 'Elixir') read off the manifests — not a stack essay. validate blocks it on a subdomain (a bounded context has no stack).

tech_source.description: optional bare path:line anchor to the manifest line proving the tech label (go.mod, package.json, pyproject.toml).

capability.description: the capability this use case belongs to, or null. Assigned at synthesis via `reconcile` (a `CAP<n>` does not exist when the behavioral fragment is written).

entry_points.description: the TRIGGER arm of entry-point claiming: the front door(s) an actor hits to START this use case. Empty is legitimate — the surface may sit inside a coarse T4 row a sibling already names.

id.description: this step's position in the ordered walk.

uc.description: the use case this step realizes.

why.description: the prerequisite that fixes this step's position — why it can't come earlier in the walk.

subsystem.description: the owning subsystem's id, or null if ungrouped.

entry_point.description: bare `path:line` anchor: a repo-relative file path, optionally followed by `:line` or `:line-line` — never a markdown link (its label would just be the basename, fully derivable from the path, so it is never authored). Where the component is TRIGGERED — distinct from `source` (where it LIVES).

source.description: either a bare file `path:line` anchor (see `evidence[].file`'s description) or a bare directory ref ending in `/`. Where the component LIVES.

confidence.description: verified = read in the code; inferred = deduced. '' = unstated.

files.description: repo-relative file paths this component owns, as a plain list — not a count, not a comma-joined string.

extra.description: freeform authored columns — any JSON value, agent-chosen keys. The ONE place with no fixed meaning: a key `coyodex validate` gives an enforced shape to, or that the method documents as a convention, graduates to a real field instead and is then rejected here under its old spelling (this is how `files`/`evidence`/`package`/`alternative` were promoted).

file.description: bare `path:line` anchor: a repo-relative file path, optionally followed by `:line` or `:line-line` — never a markdown link (its label would just be the basename, fully derivable from the path, so it is never authored).

why.description: why this citation supports the claim — what a skeptic re-reading `file` should find true.

states.description: the declared state names — non-empty, unique; never synthesized (record only a lifecycle the code implements in an enum / status constants / dispatch table).

source.description: bare path:line anchor to the line DECLARING the states; '' = inferred (advisory).

on.description: the trigger label ('connect ok', 'refresh failed'); optional.

kind.description: closed Context vocabulary; null → inferred from `type`.

bucket.description: PURPOSE bucket (seeded-open) grouping the dep within its diagram — external systems in Context, in-process code in the Libraries drill. Prefer a seed (Data & storage, Identity & access, Observability, Messaging & delivery, AI & ML, Infrastructure & runtime, Integrations for external systems; Web framework / server, Frontend / UI, Data drivers, Service SDKs, Validation / models, Logging, Crypto / security for libraries); mint a new one only when none fits. Empty → inferred from `type` + `used_for`.

where_configured.description: bare `path:line` anchor: a repo-relative file path, optionally followed by `:line` or `:line-line` — never a markdown link (its label would just be the basename, fully derivable from the path, so it is never authored).

confidence.description: verified = read in the code; inferred = deduced. '' = unstated.

alternative.description: the fallback used instead of this dep, and under what circumstance.

extra.description: freeform authored columns — any JSON value, agent-chosen keys. The ONE place with no fixed meaning: a key `coyodex validate` gives an enforced shape to, or that the method documents as a convention, graduates to a real field instead and is then rejected here under its old spelling (this is how `files`/`evidence`/`package`/`alternative` were promoted).

source.description: bare `path:line` anchor: a repo-relative file path, optionally followed by `:line` or `:line-line` — never a markdown link (its label would just be the basename, fully derivable from the path, so it is never authored). Where the run command is defined — the script, Makefile target, or config line the action runs.

id.description: MINTED BY `assemble` from content (source + trigger + owner + kind), never authored — leave it out of a fragment. Change-impact keeps its own content key (`ep:{source}`), which is stable across rebuilds where a minted number is not.

kind.description: what the entry point IS — a SEEDED-OPEN vocabulary (never blocking): prefer a seed (http-route, ui-route, cli, webhook, mcp-tool, middleware, job, poller, event-consumer, startup-hook, signal-handler); mint a project-specific kind only when none fits, and reuse the exact spelling on rebuild (validate folds known drift like 'http'→'http-route' and nudges the rest).

source.description: bare `path:line` anchor: a repo-relative file path, optionally followed by `:line` or `:line-line` — never a markdown link (its label would just be the basename, fully derivable from the path, so it is never authored).

activation.description: who starts it: 'self' (timer/loop/boot/signal/queue consumer — runs with no caller) or 'external' (route/CLI/callback/webhook); '' → inferred from `kind`.

cadence.description: WHEN a self-activated entry point runs: a cron expression ('0 3 * * *'), an interval ('every 30s'), 'on-boot', or 'continuous'. Meaningful only when the effective activation is 'self' (a cadence on an external EP draws an advisory).

cadence_source.description: bare path:line anchor to the line DECLARING the schedule (beat/cron config, compose, the loop's sleep) — often a different line than `source`; '' on a set cadence = inferred (advisory).

subdomain.description: the owning subdomain's id, or null if ungrouped.

source.description: either a bare file `path:line` anchor (see `evidence[].file`'s description) or a bare directory ref ending in `/`. Must anchor the entity's actual type DEFINITION (the `class X`/`@dataclass` line), never a use site.

dep.description: the physical datastore/messaging dep holding this entity (a D-id); null for a store with no dep (in-memory, in-code registry).

container.description: the compartment inside the dep: collection / table / key prefix / bucket / file name.

mode.description: how the entity relates to its store — closed vocabulary, exact match: collection (own compartment) / embedded (inside a parent's row) / projection (a read view over rows another entity owns) / transient / cache / in-code / enum; '' = unstated.

notes.description: what the shape can't say: TTL, cache tiers, compression.

markers.description: annotation tokens, not free text: PK / FK→En / unique / ? / [].

verb.description: contains / has / isA (structural, canonical) or a free association verb.

keyed_by.description: storage key name(s) the store uses to relate the two — a lookup/partition key it imposes, NOT a field on EITHER entity's row. Use ONLY when no field backs the link; if a field carries the id (marked FK or a plain same-named column) that is a (reverse) foreign key, not a key. Drawn on the arrow with the «key» marker.

source.description: either a bare file `path:line` anchor (see `evidence[].file`'s description) or a bare directory ref ending in `/`. Where the deliberately-unmodelled type is defined.

src.description: an element id, or a Role display name (an actor step).

where.description: bare `path:line` anchor: a repo-relative file path, optionally followed by `:line` or `:line-line` — never a markdown link (its label would just be the basename, fully derivable from the path, so it is never authored). THE location: this step's own call site — a step is exactly one interaction, so its anchor is precise (unlike an edge's `where`, an example). Required on element↔element steps unless `no_call_site`.

no_call_site.description: explicit opt-out (mirrors Edge.no_call_site): this step has no single call site — `where` may be null.

subflow.description: a REFERENCE step: 'runs SFn here'. src/dst stay authored (the run's entry/exit endpoints); `phrase` may be empty (defaults to the sub-flow's name); the step carries no `where`/`no_call_site` of its own. One level only — a sub-flow's step may not itself reference a sub-flow.

name.description: what the shared sequence does — a single verb phrase, like a use-case name.

why.description: the relationship's rationale — distinct from either endpoint's own `purpose`.

where.description: bare `path:line` anchor: a repo-relative file path, optionally followed by `:line` or `:line-line` — never a markdown link (its label would just be the basename, fully derivable from the path, so it is never authored). A verified EXAMPLE call site — one line in `src`'s code where it invokes `dst`, possibly one of many (a witness grounding the edge, not a catalog of its traffic).

name.description: unique channel/queue/topic name — the row's key (name-keyed like a deployment unit; nothing points at a channel).

kind.description: seeded-open: queue / topic / stream / pubsub / job-queue; mint a project-specific kind when none fits.

broker.description: the messaging/datastore dep carrying the channel; '' = in-process.

payload.description: the entity a message carries; '' = untyped/none.

source.description: bare path:line anchor to where the channel NAME is declared.

env.description: the environment this deployment unit runs in — must name a `environments` entry.

source.description: bare `path:line` anchor: a repo-relative file path, optionally followed by `:line` or `:line-line` — never a markdown link (its label would just be the basename, fully derivable from the path, so it is never authored). The manifest line that PLACES the unit in this environment (the compose `profiles:` line, the overlay/values file, the stage). Empty string = INFERRED (no manifest witness): `validate` surfaces it as an advisory, never blocks; a CITED source that doesn't resolve IS a hard block under `--check-sources`.

bare `path:line` anchor: a repo-relative file path, optionally followed by `:line` or `:line-line` — never a markdown link (its label would just be the basename, fully derivable from the path, so it is never authored). The auth check in code (the enforcement site).

confidence.description: verified = read in the code; inferred = deduced. '' = unstated.

statement.description: ONE product decision, in product language and naming no component — the sharp test is 'could a product person have decided otherwise?'. Two claims joined by 'and' are two rules.

name.description: the SHORT title — a few words a reader scans, the way a use case has a name beside its trigger→outcome sentence ("Owner-only cancellation"). Not a shortened statement: name the DECISION, then state it in full in `statement`.

block.description: the decision area this rule belongs to, or null. Assigned at synthesis via `reconcile` (a `BLK<n>` does not exist when the rule is authored), exactly as `use_cases[].capability` is.

sites.description: every place the decision is ENFORCED. The rule's components, its use-case steps and whether it has been swept are DERIVED from these — there is no authored field for any of them.

access.description: this rule governs WHO MAY DO WHAT — the security marker. The security surface table and the eval's auth coverage read it.

risk.description: what is AT STAKE if this decision is wrong or absent — a judgement, not a derivation. Distinct from a site's `why` (what that LINE does): a risk note says what the decision's limit costs. Rendered in the security surface table for an `access` rule.

confidence.description: verified = read in the code; inferred = deduced. '' = unstated.

where.description: bare `path:line` anchor: a repo-relative file path, optionally followed by `:line` or `:line-line` — never a markdown link (its label would just be the basename, fully derivable from the path, so it is never authored). The OPERATIVE line — the one that acts. A definition header, an import, a comment or a blank line is a shape error, not a site, and the `:line` is REQUIRED: without it the operative-line check is skipped and the claim cannot be falsified. null (with `no_call_site`) = enforced by construction, no single line.

why.description: what this line does FOR the rule ('rejects a non-owner caller') — reconstructible from the line itself, with no clause added.

no_call_site.description: explicit opt-out (mirrors Edge.no_call_site): this rule is enforced by construction (a type, a schema constraint, a config-wired guard) — `where` may be empty.
